readme:
# Vivino Wines Scraper

Get wines from [Vivino](https://www.vivino.com/) by country, wine type, rating, price range, grape and region. The actor returns one record per vintage: name, year, winery, region, grapes, average rating and number of ratings, bottle price and size, taste profile, food pairings and images. No login and no API key are needed.

## What you get

- One record per wine vintage, 24 per page of results.
- Filters for country and currency, wine type (red, white, sparkling, rose, dessert, fortified), minimum rating, price range, grapes and regions.
- Sorting by number of ratings, rating, or price.
- Large runs of thousands of wines. When you ask for more than 10,000 wines the actor reads the results price band by band and drops wines that show up twice.
- Each wine once per run. A run that is interrupted continues where it stopped. Wines already delivered are not delivered or charged again.
- You pay only for wines that were saved to the dataset.

## Use with AI agents (MCP)

Connect this actor to any MCP-compatible AI client, such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, LangChain or LlamaIndex.

**MCP server URL:**

```
https://mcp.apify.com?tools=santamaria-automations/vivino-wines-scraper
```

**Example prompt once connected:**

> "Use `vivino-wines-scraper` to list the 50 most rated red wines between 15 and 40 dollars with their rating, price and grapes as a CSV."

## Data extracted

| Field | Example |
|-------|---------|
| `vintage_id` | `1469112` |
| `wine_id` | `1136137` |
| `url` | `"https://www.vivino.com/w/1136137"`, with `?year=2023` added when the vintage has a year |
| `name` | `"Meiomi Pinot Noir"` |
| `wine_name` | `"Pinot Noir"` |
| `year`, `is_non_vintage` | `null`, `false` (`is_non_vintage` is true for wines listed as N.V.; some wines list no year) |
| `winery_id`, `winery_name`, `winery_url` | `199777`, `"Meiomi"`, `"https://www.vivino.com/wineries/meiomi"` |
| `wine_type`, `wine_type_id` | `"red"`, `1` |
| `is_natural` | `false` |
| `region`, `region_id` | `"California"`, `24` |
| `country`, `country_code` | `"United States"`, `"US"` |
| `grapes` | `["Pinot Noir"]` |
| `style_name`, `style_id` | `"Californian Pinot Noir"`, `157` |
| `body`, `body_description` | `3`, `"Medium-bodied"` |
| `acidity`, `acidity_description` | `3`, `"High"` |
| `food_pairings` | `["Beef", "Veal", "Poultry"]` |
| `taste_structure` | acidity, intensity, sweetness, tannin and fizziness on a 0 to 5 scale, with the number of people behind it |
| `flavor_groups` | flavor families with their most named keywords |
| `rating_average`, `ratings_count` | `4.1`, `187241` |
| `wine_rating_average`, `wine_ratings_count` | rating across all years of the wine |
| `labels_count` | number of scanned labels |
| `price_amount`, `price_currency` | `15.99`, `"USD"` |
| `price_before_discount`, `discount_percent` | set when the offer is discounted |
| `bottle_size_ml`, `bottle_type` | `750`, `"Bottle (0.75l)"` |
| `price_url` | address of the offer page |
| `image_url`, `bottle_image_url` | label and bottle images |
| `query` | the filters the row was found with |
| `page` | result page the row came from |
| `scraped_at` | `"2026-11-07T10:00:00Z"` |

Fields that Vivino does not show for a wine are returned empty. Grapes come from the wine style, so a few wines have none.

## Pricing

Pay-per-event pricing. You pay only for wines that were saved to the dataset.

| Event | Price |
|-------|-------|
| Actor start (`actor-start`) | $0.001 per run |
| Wine scraped (`wine-result`) | $0.003 per wine ($3.00 per 1,000) |

The start event is charged once per run, together with the first saved wine. A run that returns nothing is not charged. If you set a maximum cost per run, the actor stops before it goes over that limit.

## Input

| Field | Type | Description | Default |
|-------|------|-------------|---------|
| `countryCode` | string | Market whose offers and prices are listed, for example `US`, `GB`, `DE`, `FR`, `CH`. | `US` |
| `currencyCode` | string | Currency for prices, for example `USD`, `EUR`, `GBP`. Empty uses the usual currency of the country. | by country |
| `wineTypes` | string[] | `red`, `white`, `sparkling`, `rose`, `dessert`, `fortified`. Empty includes all types. | all |
| `minRating` | number | Lowest average rating, 1 to 5. | `1` |
| `priceMin` | number | Lowest bottle price. | `0` |
| `priceMax` | number | Highest bottle price. 0 or empty uses 500. | `500` |
| `grapeIds` | string[] | Vivino grape numbers, for example `2` (Cabernet Sauvignon), `14` (Pinot Noir), `5` (Chardonnay). | none |
| `regionIds` | string[] | Vivino region numbers. Every result has its `region_id`. | none |
| `sortBy` | string | `ratings_count`, `ratings_average`, `price_low_to_high` or `price_high_to_low`. | `ratings_count` |
| `maxItems` | integer | Most wines to return. 0 uses 100. | `100` |

## Usage examples

### 48 popular red and white wines between 10 and 60 dollars

```json
{
  "countryCode": "US",
  "wineTypes": ["red", "white"],
  "minRating": 3.5,
  "priceMin": 10,
  "priceMax": 60,
  "maxItems": 48
}
```

### Highest rated sparkling wines in euros

```json
{
  "countryCode": "DE",
  "currencyCode": "EUR",
  "wineTypes": ["sparkling"],
  "sortBy": "ratings_average",
  "minRating": 4,
  "maxItems": 100
}
```

### A deep list across all prices

```json
{
  "countryCode": "US",
  "priceMax": 1000,
  "maxItems": 15000
}
```

## Output

Results are saved to the default dataset. Export them as JSON, CSV or Excel, or read them through the API.

```json
{
  "vintage_id": 1469112,
  "wine_id": 1136137,
  "url": "https://www.vivino.com/w/1136137",
  "name": "Meiomi Pinot Noir",
  "year": null,
  "is_non_vintage": false,
  "winery_name": "Meiomi",
  "wine_type": "red",
  "region": "California",
  "country": "United States",
  "grapes": ["Pinot Noir"],
  "style_name": "Californian Pinot Noir",
  "rating_average": 4.1,
  "ratings_count": 187241,
  "price_amount": 15.99,
  "price_currency": "USD",
  "bottle_size_ml": 750
}
```

## Limitations

- Prices and offers depend on the market (`countryCode`). The same wine can show a different price, or none, in another country, and the offer can differ a little between runs.
- A wine without an offer in the chosen market has an empty price.
- Sorting by price orders by the lowest offer Vivino lists.
- Only the list data is read. The actor does not return the text of user reviews, user profiles or price history.
- Grape lists, taste profile and food pairings are shown by Vivino only for some wines. Those fields are empty for the rest.
- The number of wines Vivino shows for a query changes over time and with the market, so two runs a day apart can differ.
- For runs over 10,000 wines the order of results follows the price bands, not one global ranking.

## FAQ

**How many wines can I get?**
Vivino lists tens of thousands of wines per market. Set `maxItems` to the number you need. Each page of results holds 24 wines, so 1,000 wines take about 42 requests.

**Why do some wines have no price?**
Vivino shows a price only when a seller in the chosen market offers the wine. Try another `countryCode`, or leave the price range wide.

**What do the grape and region numbers mean?**
They are Vivino's own numbers. Every result carries its `region_id`, so you can run one query, read the region numbers from the results, and filter by them in the next run. The grape names appear in `grapes`.

**What does a run cost?**
The pricing table shows a start fee plus a price per 1,000 wines. A run of 48 wines costs a start fee plus 48 wines.

**What status does a run end with?**
The run status says how many wines were delivered. If Vivino refuses every request, the run fails and nothing is charged. If the filters match no wines, the run ends normally and says so.

**Does it need a Vivino account?**
No. The actor reads the same public lists that the Vivino explore page shows.
